questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) Describe and give an example for each term

(i) Utility software. (3 marks)

(ii) Device driver. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Utility software (3 marks)**

Utility software is system software that performs maintenance and housekeeping tasks which help to keep the computer working well (it is not used to produce documents). **Examples:** an antivirus program (finds and removes viruses), a disk defragmenter or disk cleaner, a back-up program, a file compression program (such as WinZip).

**(ii) Device driver (3 marks)**

A device driver is a small program that lets the operating system communicate with, and control, a particular hardware device, by translating the general commands of the operating system into commands that the device understands. Without its driver, the device cannot work correctly. **Examples:** a printer driver, a graphics (video) card driver, a keyboard or scanner driver.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) Explain the difference between:

(i) Object-oriented and procedural programming paradigms. (2 marks)

(ii) Sequence and choice constructs in algorithm design. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Object-oriented and procedural programming (2 marks)**

- In **procedural programming** a program is a series of procedures (functions) that are called in turn; the data and the procedures are separate, and the program is built by dividing the task into smaller procedures (examples: C, Pascal).
- In **object-oriented programming** the program is built from **objects** that combine the data (attributes) and the procedures that work on it (methods) in one unit called a class; it uses ideas such as encapsulation, inheritance and polymorphism (examples: Java, C++, Python).

**(ii) Sequence and choice (2 marks)**

- A **sequence** is a set of instructions carried out one after the other, in the order in which they are written, without skipping any.
- A **choice (selection)** is a decision: a condition is tested, and one set of instructions or another is carried out depending on whether the condition is true or false (IF ... THEN ... ELSE, CASE).
